responses:
## Analysis

Three earlier attempts restructured the tail dispatch in different ways and all produced exactly the same cost (3836). That suggests the cost is dominated by the per-word work, not by the branch layout of the tail. The remaining per-word overhead comes from the 16 `bits.OnesCount64` calls per block. In giri, each call is a function invocation whose body is itself a sequence of SSA instructions, so every word pays call overhead on top of the popcount arithmetic.

## Proposed change

Inline the SWAR popcount in the 16-word main loop, so no calls are made there. The per-word steps are the standard ones:

1. `x -= (x>>1) & m1`
2. `x = (x & m2) + ((x>>2) & m2)`
3. `x = (x + (x>>4)) & m4`

After step 3, each byte lane holds a count between 0 and 8. Summing 16 such words keeps each byte lane at most 128, so the lanes cannot overflow. One fold then reduces the byte lanes to 16-bit lanes (each at most 256). Multiplying by `0x0001000100010001` and shifting right by 48 yields the sum of all four 16-bit lanes, which is at most 1024 and therefore fits without carries.

The tail dispatch is left unchanged. Because the function still reads the same words and returns the same count, correctness is preserved. Whether this lowers the cost depends on how giri charges call overhead, so the gain is uncertain. It is worth testing against the 3836 baseline.
